messages:
megan: Heads-up — canary rolled out for the strict fncall validator and we started seeing a spike of customer errors in the console (~0.8% of calls). Dashboard shows most rejects are inbound third-party adapters returning slightly different shapes. Anyone owning routing vs validator policy?

thomas: I can take routing policy, but not the validator. From the dashboard it looks like majority are array vs object mismatches (tools returning arrays for results).

anika: Validator owner here. We intentionally flipped strict -> reject for canary to measure noise. Did we set sampling on the reject telemetry? Need to confirm we aren't overcounting.

megan: @anika sampling is default 100% for canary. We wanted visibility. Ops wants to reduce pager noise.

chen: Example payload we saw in logs (parsing failure):
```json
{"tool_call": "search", "output": ["id", 123], "meta": {"source": "partner-x"}}
```
The validator expects `output` to be an object: `{id: number, text: string}`. So adapters that changed shape are failing.

anika: Hmm. A couple options: 1) revert canary -> permissive for now, 2) keep strict but add a soft-fail path that records metric and continues, or 3) route traffic for partners flagged as legacy to a compatibility variant.

thomas: (2) sounds safest operationally — we keep telemetry for regression detection but avoid user-facing failures. Can we tag route metadata so console groups by `partner`?

megan: We need an immediate mitigation and then a plan. Short term: switch validator to "log-and-pass" for the canary slice. Long term: routing rule that pins legacy partners to the compatibility model.

anika: I can push a hotfix to the validator today — toggle `soft_validate` for the canary route id. Patch will set metric `fncall.strict_rejects` to increment but return a 200 with `tool_passthrough: true` so callers don't see errors.

thomas: For routing, I'll draft a small firewall rule: if metadata.partner in legacy_list -> route to `tool-compat-v1`. That avoids touching partner infra.

megan: Ops: can we add a dashboard panel that splits rejects by `partner` and `route_id` and marks the canary slice? Right now it's per-model which hides partner skew.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary toggle change requested by @anika. CI job queued. ETA ~12m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

chen: One more ask — capture a sample of failing payloads (redact PII) and store in `fncall/reject-samples/` for triage. Without samples we keep guessing.

anika: Agreed. I'll add a sampling hook to dump 1% of rejects to that bucket with partner and route tags. Will also add a note in the console changelog explaining we temporarily softened validation.

megan: Thanks. Follow-ups: @thomas please check routing rule for performance implications; @chen collect initial sample set and flag top 5 partner offenders; @anika push soft-validate hotfix and then we'll re-evaluate after 24h.

thomas: Got it. Will ping if CPU on routing proxy spikes.

chen: Will start pulling samples now.

anika: Patch merged, canary soft-validate on. Telemetry shows rejects still captured but no client errors. Will post a short postmortem tomorrow with numbers.

megan: Great — closing the loop here. We'll follow up in product weekly about whether to do compatibility routing or require partner upgrades. :white_check_mark:
